issues.legal_issue: A conditional undertaking to complete a sale takes effect when the specified settlement confirms the seller’s ownership and entitlement to possession, and a conveyance to another person not contemplated by that settlement breaches the sale obligations.
material_facts: The parties had agreed to sell a plot, and the purchaser later agreed to pay the remaining price and take a conveyance if the seller’s ownership was confirmed and possession obtained through settlement of pending litigation.
The litigation was decreed in the seller’s favour for ownership and delivery of possession; the decree did not provide for a sale to the subsequent purchasers.
Before the decree was passed, the sellers conveyed the plot to the subsequent purchasers, who claimed through a person involved in the litigation.
issues.conclusion: The conditional undertaking took effect on the decree, and the earlier conveyance to the subsequent purchasers breached the sellers’ contractual obligations.
issues.legal_principle: The court construed the later undertaking according to its terms and in conjunction with the original sale agreement. Because the specified condition was satisfied by a decree confirming ownership and entitlement to possession, a different conveyance that was not contemplated by that decree did not constitute the settlement described in the undertaking. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.sale_contract_dispute: The proceeding concerns enforcement of an agreement to sell property.
predicates.conditional_sale_undertaking: The purchaser agreed to complete the purchase if a specified outcome in pending litigation confirmed the seller’s ownership and entitlement to possession.
predicates.settlement_confirms_ownership_and_posses: The outcome of the pending litigation confirms the seller’s ownership and entitlement to possession.
predicates.later_conveyance_not_contemplated_by_set: The seller conveys the property to another person in a manner not provided for by the settlement or outcome specified in the undertaking.
predicates.sellers_breached_contract: The sellers’ conduct amounts to a breach of their contractual obligations.

issues.definition: When a sale-contract dispute involves a conditional undertaking and the specified settlement confirms ownership and possession, a conveyance not contemplated by that settlement means the sellers breached the contract.

issues.legal_issue: Specific performance should not be refused where the claimant acted fairly and the circumstances do not establish equitable grounds for withholding that relief.
material_facts: The purchaser acted fairly and there was no evidence that he encouraged the sellers to convey the property to the subsequent purchasers.
There was no evidence that the purchaser obtained an unfair advantage or that performance would cause the respondents unforeseen hardship.

The subsequent purchasers alleged that they had built on the property, but the court was unable to find that permanent construction had been established; any building material could be removed when possession was delivered.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser was entitled to specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: The ordinary rule is that specific performance should be granted and should be denied only when equitable considerations point to refusal and damages would constitute adequate relief. The court applied that principle to the claimant’s conduct and the evidence of hardship and construction. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and claimant_acted_fairly and no_unfair_advantage and no_unforeseen_hardship and permanent_construction_not_proven

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding seeks enforcement of an agreement by requiring conveyance of property.
predicates.claimant_acted_fairly: The claimant acted fairly in relation to the agreement and its performance.
predicates.no_unfair_advantage: There is no evidence that the claimant secured an unfair advantage when entering the agreement.
predicates.no_unforeseen_hardship: There is no evidence that performance would impose unforeseen hardship on the opposing parties.
predicates.permanent_construction_not_proven: The evidence does not establish that permanent construction was made on the property.
predicates.specific_performance_granted: The agreement is enforced by an order requiring its performance.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance suit, fair conduct and the absence of proven unfair advantage, unforeseen hardship, and permanent construction support granting specific performance.

issues.legal_issue: A sum stipulated for breach does not make damages an alternative to specific performance when the stipulation is intended only to secure performance.
material_facts: The sellers relied on a clause in the sale contract providing for payment of damages in case of breach.
The court found from the contract’s terms that the clause was included to secure performance, not to give the sellers an option to pay money instead of performing.
issues.conclusion: The damages clause did not prevent the purchaser from seeking enforcement of the agreement by specific performance.
issues.legal_principle: A stipulated sum for breach does not bar specific performance when, on the construction of the contract, it serves to secure performance rather than provide the promisor an option to pay damages instead. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The proceeding seeks enforcement of an agreement by requiring conveyance of property.
predicates.breach_sum_clause: The agreement specifies a sum payable in the event of breach.
predicates.clause_secures_performance_only: The agreement shows that the stipulated sum is intended to secure performance and not to give the promisor an option to pay instead of performing.
predicates.damages_clause_does_not_exclude_specific: The stipulated sum does not prevent the court from ordering specific performance.

issues.definition: Where a specific-performance suit concerns an agreement with a breach sum clause intended only to secure performance, the clause does not exclude specific performance.

issues.legal_issue: An objection that the property is not sufficiently identified may be rejected when it was not raised in the pleadings and the parties were not in doubt about the property’s identity.
material_facts: The respondents argued on appeal that the land was not sufficiently defined in the plaint and could not be identified.
The objection had not been raised in the pleadings, and the parties had not been in doubt about the identity of the disputed land.
issues.conclusion: The court declined to allow the identification objection to be raised at that stage.
issues.legal_principle: The court declined to entertain an objection first raised at that stage when it had not been pleaded and the parties had understood which property was in dispute. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.property_enforcement_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in a dispute seeking enforcement concerning property.
predicates.identity_objection_not_pleaded: A party raises an objection that the property is not identifiable even though that objection was not raised in the pleadings.
predicates.property_identity_not_in_doubt: The parties were not in doubt about which property was the subject of the dispute.
predicates.late_identity_objection_rejected: The court declines to entertain the identification objection at that stage.

issues.definition: In a property-enforcement appeal, an unpleaded identification objection is rejected when the parties were not in doubt about the property’s identity.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal is not barred by limitation when the party asserting the bar has not proved that the appeal is out of time.
material_facts: A party contended that the appeal was barred by limitation.
The court found that it had not been proved that the appeal was barred.
issues.conclusion: The court did not find the appeal barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: The court rejected the limitation contention because the asserted bar had not been proved. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.limitation_bar_asserted: A party contends that the appeal was filed too late.
predicates.limitation_bar_not_proven: The evidence does not establish that the appeal was filed too late.
predicates.appeal_not_barred: The court does not treat the appeal as barred by limitation.

issues.definition: An appeal is not treated as barred when a limitation bar is asserted but not proven.
